measure_name: Project-financed climate and disaster risk assessment
definition: A project-financed climate and disaster risk assessment systematically evaluates hazards, exposure, vulnerability or potential impacts in order to inform a project activity, investment, design or operational requirement. Counts only when the project finances, commissions, carries out or explicitly requires a substantive assessment from an implementing agency, operator, consultant, contractor or bidder. The assessment may cover a site, route, asset, system, sector or investment program and may inform subsequent siting, design or operational measures, which should be classified separately. Bank appraisal-stage climate screening, CDRS, Paris Alignment analysis, climate co-benefits calculations, CCDR findings and general PAD descriptions of climate vulnerability do not count. An assessment completed outside the project does not count unless the project finances its preparation, update or substantive application as a project activity. The World Bank's screening of this project is excluded, but a screening or assessment that the project itself finances of its own or named sites, routes or investments counts. A law, rule or system requiring assessments of future investments in general is climate_governance, not this. A rule, procedure or manual requiring that future investments be assessed is climate_governance even when this project adopts it; an assessment this project carries out of specific sites, routes or subprojects counts here. A reference to "the climate risk assessment" that the project does not finance is the World Bank's screening (grade 1). The assessment must concern climate or disaster hazards: a safety, security, market or economic-opportunity assessment is not this.
boundary: The project assesses climate or disaster risk.
note: Deliberately excludes generic “climate screening” language because it is heavily contaminated by Bank appraisal processes. Positive classification requires a project activity or requirement, not evidence that the Bank assessed the project. v4 (2026-10-20): Dev's revision; measures are defined by the intervention, the asset map gives the asset. v5 (2026-10-21): grade 1 adds existing systems, results-framework indicators, economic-analysis assumptions and other World Bank projects; types rewritten to exclude each other and asked as one choice. v6 (2026-10-21, Dev's graded sheet): hedged wording is grade 2; benefit claims, examples and other donors are grade 1; boundary lines from the graders' notes; commit_floor from the graded sheet. v7 (2026-10-21, Dev's s4 sheet and a review of it): scales say how examples, technical assistance, training and hedges grade; an unfinanced "the climate risk assessment" is the Bank's screening; the assessment must be about climate or disaster hazards.
